subject: Burst quota & autoscale escrow proposal — Cascade Therapeutics

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: burst quota escrow model for Cascade Therapeutics (DEAL-1729)

Hi Ben / Marcus,

Cascade (Alex Reed) is asking for a predictable burst allowance on top of their Dedicated commit. They want a mechanism that:

- Guarantees a baseline committed slab (as negotiated in the PO).
- Allows temporary 2–3x uplift for brief periods (1–3 hours) without application failures.
- Caps monthly burst spend and provides an escrow / crediting mechanism so they only pay for true overages.

Attached is a usage snapshot they sent (cascade-usage-snapshot.csv) showing weekly peaks that are roughly 2.7x their committed 24/7 baseline but last <3 hours. Their ask: a contractual burst pool with pre-authorized capacity and an escrow repayment plan tied to usage.

Questions for the team:
1) Can we specify a burst tiering model that limits continuous burst to X hours per day and Y hours per month?
2) What eviction / preemption behavior will we expose for burst workloads—best-effort vs. protected?
3) What guardrails do we need operationally (alerts, throttles, automatic fallback to smaller model) to avoid SLA hits for other dedicated customers?

I sketched a starting point in the attached PDF (proposed-burst-tier.pdf) but need input on the ops implications (Aditya), commercial wording (Ben), and CS impact (Monica).

Goal: get a procurement-ready addendum we can send to Cascade by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: burst quota escrow model for Cascade Therapeutics (DEAL-1729)

Thanks Jasmine — good summary. A couple quick thoughts before we loop Cascade back:

- Commercial framing: call it “Burst Credit Pool + Escrow” and surface a monthly cap and a soft daily cap. The escrow can be a holding credit equal to one month of average burst usage (we can amortize if they prefer).
- Pricing: we should price burst tokens at 1.6x hosted unit rate for dedicated to reflect higher ops cost.
- Billing: prefer a lagged invoicing approach (monthly) with the escrow balance settling quarterly.

Operational asks for Aditya / Marcus: please confirm whether we can:
  a) enforce a per-job max allocation so a single job can't consume the entire pool;
  b) offer two modes—protected burst (no preemption but higher cost, limited hours) and best-effort burst (preemptible with lower cost).

Marcus — can you draft a short tech appendix describing eviction behavior, preemption signals, and how fallback to smaller models would be orchestrated?

If we can land this commercial language, Monica can prepare the CS runbook for onboarding.

Ben
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Reed <alex@cascade.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-01T08:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: burst quota escrow model for Cascade Therapeutics (DEAL-1729)

Hi Jasmine / Ben — thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications from our side (per procurement):

- Our burst profile: most of our peaks are predictable (batch ingest windows M/W/F 02:00–05:00 UTC) and occasional ad-hoc model re-runs after product pushes. Peaks historically ~2.5–3x baseline for ~1–3 hours.
- We absolutely want protected burst for the ingest windows (we can commit to a weekly schedule) and can accept best-effort for ad-hoc runs.
- We'd prefer an escrow equal to ~2 weeks of projected burst consumption rather than a full month if that helps the cashflow on our side.
- SLA ask: during protected burst, we expect latency SLOs not to degrade beyond 1.25x baseline. If that can't be guaranteed, we need a lower price tier for protected burst.

I attached the usage snapshot you referenced (cascade-usage-snapshot.csv) and a brief note from our SREs that explains their patterns.

Can you also confirm: who at Redwood will be the technical owner for configuring the scheduled protected windows? We want to coordinate a recurring sync to lock the weekly schedule.

Thanks — Alex
VP of ML Platforms — Cascade Therapeutics
Attachments: cascade-usage-snapshot.csv (CSV, 28KB)

Subject: Re: Proposal: burst quota & autoscale escrow model for Cascade Therapeutics (DEAL-1729)

Alex — appreciated the usage detail. A few operational notes (outline + proposed defaults) — see attached proposed-burst-tier.pdf for a formatted version.

Summary / proposed defaults:
- Tiering: 3 burst levels — Protected Scheduled (PS), Protected On-Demand (POD, limited approvals), Best-effort (BE).
- Hour caps: PS: up to 4 hours per scheduled window, up to 12 hours/week; POD: up to 6 hours/month; BE: unlimited but preemptible.
- Preemption policy: BE instances are preempted with a 30s SIGTERM + 2 minute drain; POD/PS are not preempted but consume from the escrow pool at the protected rate.
- Fairness: per-tenant job cap enforced (max concurrent GPUs per job) and per-pool reservations to prevent a single tenant job from draining the entire shared burst slab.
- Fallbacks: when protected pool is exhausted, we will: 1) attempt routing to alternate region if capacity exists; 2) if no region capacity, throttle requests and return a 503 with JSON payload advising retry/backoff and offering a smaller model variant.

Metrics & alerts:
- We will emit burst-pool-usage (per minute), pool-eviction-rate, and protected-fallback-rate to the Console; set default alerts at 80% and 95% pool consumption.

Implementation plan & owner:
- Aditya to own implementation of the per-job caps, preemption hooks, and alerting.
- Marcus to own deployment knobs and rollback policy; will test with a canary internal tenant for 2 weeks.

If these defaults look OK commercially, Ben/Monica, we can convert them into contractual appendix language.

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Burst quota & autoscale escrow proposal — Cascade Therapeutics (DEAL-1729)

Alex / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turn. Based on Marcus and Aditya's input, here is the agreed draft we can put into an addendum:

Key commercial points (draft):
- Burst Credit Pool + Escrow: Redwood will provision a burst pool sized to allow up to 3x baseline for scheduled windows (up to 4 hours per window, up to 12 hours/week). Cascade will fund an escrow equal to two weeks of projected burst consumption; monthly settlements thereafter.
- Pricing: Protected burst usage billed at 1.5x base dedicated token rate; best-effort billed at 1.0x base dedicated token rate. (Ben: if you can confirm the final multiplier we will update the pdf).
- Failover & throttling: If protected pool is exhausted and cross-region capacity is unavailable, Redwood will throttle and offer fallback to smaller model variants; Redwood will provide 503 responses with guidance payloads.
- SLA: During scheduled Protected windows Redwood will target latency degradation <1.25x baseline; credits apply if window-level availability drops below 99.5% (TBD in addendum).

Operational next steps:
1) Marcus / Aditya to schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff (owner: Aditya).
2) Monica to draft onboarding runbook and playbook for scheduled windows.
3) Jasmine to circulate addendum for review and start the DocuSign flow.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deals/1729
- DocuSign draft: https://app.docusign.com/signon/claim?doc=burst-addendum

Please reply with any redlines by EOD Friday. If no redlines, Procurement — can you confirm acceptance and we'll send the DocuSign invite?

Thanks,
Jasmine
